headline: Six straight defeats and still favourites: Norwich at Charlton
summary: Norwich arrive at The Valley on Saturday lunchtime with 6 straight Championship defeats behind them, their manager Philippe Clement under pressure — and still the market's favourites. Top scorer Toure is out with a shoulder injury, and the visitors create only 0.73 expected goals a game. Charlton are winless in 8, and Nathan Jones called Saturday's Watford defeat inexcusable. What holds Norwich up is the fixture: 3 straight wins over Charlton, each by a single goal. Across the bookmakers they are 44.5% to win, against Charlton's 29.1%, but rated only 0.31 goals better — a third of a goal.
read: Two of the Championship's coldest sides meet at The Valley: Norwich have lost six straight league games, Charlton are winless in eight and their manager called Saturday's performance inexcusable. Norwich are still the market's favourites at 44.5%, rated only about a third of a goal better, with over 2.5 goals priced at 51%.

facts.fact: Norwich are the market's favourites at 44.5% to win at The Valley, against Charlton's 29.1%.
facts.meaning: The away side is favoured even though it is Charlton who sit higher in the table.

facts.fact: Norwich's 0-1 home defeat to Portsmouth was their sixth straight Championship loss, and BBC Sport reports the run has piled pressure on boss Philippe Clement.
facts.meaning: They arrive as favourites with no league win in six attempts and a manager under scrutiny.

facts.fact: Charlton are winless in eight Championship games, and Nathan Jones called Saturday's 0-2 defeat at Watford 'inexcusable'.
facts.meaning: The home side goes into the lunchtime kick-off without a win and with its manager publicly critical of the performance.

facts.fact: Norwich are 21st in the Championship with 9 points from 11 games, five fewer than Charlton in 17th.
facts.meaning: The visitors are in the bottom four and below the side they are favourites to beat.

facts.fact: Norwich are without striker M. Toure (536 minutes, six goals this season) because of a shoulder injury.
facts.meaning: A side that has scored four goals in its last five league games loses the man who scored most of them.

facts.fact: Norwich have averaged 0.73 xG per game across their last five league matches.
facts.meaning: They are creating under one expected goal a game — the results are not just bad luck.

facts.fact: Charlton's biggest absentee is N. Chalobah (317 minutes, rating 7.08), and he is only doubtful with a muscle injury.
facts.meaning: The home side is close to full strength, with the question mark in midfield rather than in attack.

facts.fact: Norwich have won the last three meetings between the clubs, including 0-1 at The Valley in March.
facts.meaning: Recent history in this fixture is all Norwich, in a game between two sides short of wins.

sources.fact: Charlton's 0-2 defeat at Watford extended their winless run to eight games and dropped them to seventeenth in the Championship.
Nathan Jones did not spare his side criticism after the 0-2 defeat at Watford, describing the performance as inexcusable.
Charlton fan writer Paul Sullivan said the Addicks are 'too accommodating' amid their slide down the table after defeat by Watford.
Charlton drew 2-2 at Burnley a week ago, Ivan Mesik equalising in the 96th minute.
South London Sport reports that Charlton and Norwich are both badly in need of victory in Saturday's lunchtime kick-off, and looks at potential changes Nathan Jones could make.
Charlton fans have called on fellow Addicks to 'be the 12th man' against Norwich, acknowledging the side's poor performances this season.
Norwich's 0-1 home defeat to Portsmouth was their sixth straight loss in the Championship.
BBC Sport reports that the sixth straight defeat piled the pressure on Norwich boss Philippe Clement.
